comments.content: this issue is already taken by the other bounty hunter, pls find an issue with no assignee

This issue is really tricky
We have a [diamond contract](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/Diamond.sol) which includes all the [facets](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/tree/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets).
Each facet has a struct ([example](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibCreditNftManager.sol#L43)) which is used as a storage in a unique slot ([example](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibCreditNftManager.sol#L26)).
So on each PR we should check that:
- state variables in storage structs are not modified
- now new state variables are added in the beginning or middle of storage structs (we can add new state variables only to the end of a storage struct in order not to allow a storage collision)
- check that the same rules are also applied to the [AppStorage](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibAppStorage.sol) (which occupies slot 0 in all of the facets)
- make sure that newly added facets are also checked accordingly
So there should be a script that fetches storage layouts from all of the facets (perhaps via [forge inspect](https://book.getfoundry.sh/reference/forge/forge-inspect)) and compares the structure in the PR with the structure in the `development` branch

Regarding the libraries, we should have some function that checks that libs' structs used as a storage ([example](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/development/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibCreditNftManager.sol#L43)) do not have newly added properties in the beginning or the middle of the struct in order to eliminate storage collisions on contracts upgrade
Libs with only internal methods are included in the contracts' bytecode hence we still can get storage values via `web3. eth.getStorageAt()` or `forge inspect`: https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/v0.8.15/internals/layout_in_storage.html
Perhaps

Structs can be modified but only via addition to the end of them, you should check [this](https://proxies.yacademy.dev/pages/security-guide/#storage-collision-vulnerability) and get to know how it can be mitigated in the diamond proxy pattern

Code formatting would really help
Yes, new variable is added to the end of the `ChefStorage` struct

There is also this [tool](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/upgrades-plugins/1.x/api-core#usage) by openzeppelin which works pretty much the same way as https://github.com/Rubilmax/foundry-storage-check. Although both tools (as far as I understand) don't support diamond proxies perhaps there is a way to somehow modify our contracts dynamically to make them compatible with those tools.

comments.content: @gitcoindev Could you elaborate on why [using a mapping](https://github.com/Rubilmax/foundry-storage-check/compare/main...gitcoindev:foundry-storage-check:main#diff-a9aa7d8f1bead33c53fb22bf0cdc4dfed1ac646ff4fbd59ac789b9b52770d3c0R218) inside a storage struct is considered not upgrade safe? As far as I understand using mappings in a storage struct is fine and upgrade safe.

@gitcoindev 
Works fine for the following cases:
- success: new variable is added to the end of a storage struct
- fail: new variable introduced in the beginning or in the middle of a storage struct
- fail: type of state variable changed
- fail: existing state variable removed from the middle of a storage struct
- fail: LibAppStorage should follow the same diamond layout safe rules
The following cases didn't work as expected (or there are questions regarding them):
- fail: order of state variables changed 
- fail: existing state variable removed from the end of a storage struct
- fail: inner struct is added to a storage struct. Do not put structs directly in another struct unless you don't plan on ever adding more state variables to the inner structs. You won't be able to add new state variables to inner structs in upgrades without overwriting the storage slot of variables declared after the struct. The solution is to add new state variables to the structs that are stored in mappings, rather than putting structs directly in structs, as the storage slot for variables in mappings is calculated differently and is not continuous in storage.
- fail: do not add new state variables to structs that are used in arrays. Example:
```
struct AppStorage {
  uint totalSupply;
  DoNotUpgrade[] public myArray;
}
struct DoNotUpgrade {
  ...
}
```
Questions:
1. Why do we need to [inspect](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/9d70040f76b5dbcba3ff7d05b94feffc0cc4640a/.github/workflows/diamond-storage-check.yml#L26) the `DiamondInit` contract? It is not part of any facet neither it is UUPS upgradeable.
2. This [command](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/9d70040f76b5dbcba3ff7d05b94feffc0cc4640a/.github/workflows/diamond-storage-check.yml#L28) doesn't include the [LibAccessControl](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/9d70040f76b5dbcba3ff7d05b94feffc0cc4640a/.github/workflows/diamond-storage-check.yml#L28) library in the result output. Why is it happening?
3. Why do we [include](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/9d70040f76b5dbcba3ff7d05b94feffc0cc4640a/.github/workflows/diamond-storage-check.yml#L27) the facets in the result output? Isn't it sufficient to include only the libraries?
4. Check this [commit](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/pull/30/commits/95e6b6bad198acc501bb538a582e47385aba4c82) where state variables order was updated. The [corresponding CI run](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/6300083738/job/17102154494) didn't throw any errors, only warnings. Can we throw an error in this case? It is really easy to miss the warning.
5. Check this [commit](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/pull/30/commits/718c4c43082b8c3266b4f30681fbfe90032f4d04) where state variable was removed from the end of the storage struct. The [corresponding CI run](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/6300456922/job/17103385221) didn't throw any errors or warnings. Can we throw an error in this case?
6. Check this [commit](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/pull/30/commits/2aa5542ecdc6cb4c1c7f75e8a13299ecd809ae90) where an inner struct is declared inside a storage struct. Generally we should avoid adding inner structs to storage structs because this way inner structs become not upgrade safe (i.e. we can't add new state variables to inner structs). The [corresponding CI run](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/6300584619/job/17104492043) didn't throw any errors or warnings. On the other hand we can still use inner structs (actually we already [use](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/blob/1f8fbf80b714f4c7ebbf3911e5e451530b4f146a/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibChef.sol#L53) them in some of the libs) if we 100% sure that we won't add new state variables to inner structs so I'm in doubt if we need to throw an error or simply to keep an eye on such things. What do you think?
7. Check this [commit](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/pull/30/commits/5cd474d6e1d22fdd9fabfd0f8e45adb002a5ecd6) where a dynamic array of structs is added. The [corresponding CI run](https://github.com/rndquu/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/6300919935/job/17104827148) didn't throw any errors or warnings. This [article](https://www.certik.com/resources/blog/7laIe0oZGK6IoYDwn0g2Jp-diamond-proxy-contracts-best-practices) states that we should not add new state variables to structs that are used in arrays. I don't really understand this example because from my point of view this code inside a struct `DoNotUpgrade[] public myArray;` is upgrade safe. What do you think?
P.S. Note to self: run storage check workflows only when `*.sol` files are updated

@gitcoindev Could you also elaborate on [this line](https://github.com/gitcoindev/foundry-storage-check/blob/e2e33e2073c0bf9a5b35124bc117382442b54c2d/src/input.ts#L43). Why `child.type === "ContractDefinition"` is considered to be a library?
